excerpt: A repaired car is worth less than it was. How diminished value claims work in Georgia and South Carolina, and why an appraisal beats the 17c formula.
keyTakeaways: Diminished value claims recover the loss in vehicle market value after repair. Georgia is one of the strongest DV states (State Farm v. Mabry, O.C.G.A. § 33-4-6). SC allows third-party DV claims under S.C. Code § 38-77-30. Independent appraisals beat the 17c formula.

faqs.question: What is a diminished value claim?
faqs.answer: A claim for the reduction in vehicle market value after an accident, even after full repairs.

faqs.question: Is Georgia good for DV claims?
faqs.answer: Yes. State Farm v. Mabry allows first-party claims. O.C.G.A. § 33-4-6 adds bad faith penalties.

faqs.question: Can I file in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Yes, primarily against the at-fault driver third-party insurer under S.C. Code § 38-77-30.

faqs.question: How is diminished value calculated?
faqs.answer: The 17c formula starts at 10% of NADA value with adjustments. Independent appraisals produce more accurate figures.

faqs.question: How much can I recover?
faqs.answer: Newer luxury vehicles: $5K-$20K+. Older vehicles with minor damage: $500-$2,000.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer?
faqs.answer: For claims under $3K you may handle it yourself. For larger claims or insurer pushback, an attorney negotiates more effectively.
